To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic administration of propranol is followed by a reduction in cardiac output and an increase in peripheral vascular resistance, but it is not followed by any impairment of renal function or platelet function in patients with cirrhotic portal hypertension.

chronic propranonol administration is followed in cirrhotic patients with portal hypertension and no oedema by a significant reduction of cardiac index and a parallel increase of systemic vascular resistance, but it does neither alter renal function and sodium balance, nor platelet aggregation and thromboxane A2 production during whole-blood clotting.
chronic propranonol administration is followed only by some haemodymanic alterations, which may not impair renal function in patients with cirrosis, portal hypertension and not ascites.

the effects of beta-adrenergically mediated vasodilation on the renal function in cirrhosis.
the effects of chronic propranol treatment on the haemodynamics, platelet function and renal function in patients with cirrosis, portal hypertension and without ascites.
the effects of propranol on the cardiovascular system in patients with cirrhotic portal hypertension.

the renal function is maintained during beta-adrenergy blockade in patients with compensated liver cirrhosis, because the drug does not alter the renal prostaglanding system, but rather because of the reduction of cardiac output.
propranolol is safe in patients with cirrhotic ascites and portal hypertension, and that it may be useful in the treatment of ascites.
